items.title: Chrome Emergency Patch: 7 Critical Flaws Fixed — Update Now
items.summary: Google just pushed an emergency Chrome update fixing 37 security holes — seven of them rated Critical. These are memory-corruption bugs that let a malicious website run code on your computer just by you visiting the page. No clicks needed. The affected versions are Chrome 155 bef

items.title: CISA adds four actively exploited vulnerabilities — patch Palo Alto, Cisco, Ahsay now
items.summary: CISA added four new KEV entries October 14: Palo Alto PAN-OS code injection (CVE-2026-0322), Cisco Secure Email path traversal (CVE-2026-76519), AhsayCBS auth bypass (CVE-2026-105133) and command injection (CVE-2026-105134). Check if you're affected and update at cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog

items.title: Hurricane Charity Scams Are Targeting Floridians — Here's How to Spot Them
items.summary: Hurricane season runs through November, and scammers know it. After every storm, fake charity websites, crowdfunding campaigns, and phone calls flood in — all pretending to help victims.

items.title: That 'Microsoft Support' Call Is a Scam — Hang Up Immediately
items.summary: Your phone rings. The caller says they are from Microsoft or Windows Support. They claim your computer has a virus, a security problem, or an expired license — and they need remote access to fix it. Sometimes they ask for a credit card or gift cards to "renew" your protection.
